statement: Student suggestion for the all-photos query: select * may not be needed if only the photo ID is required; select just the column you need.
detail: The teacher's reply is only "Fact, right? Okay." before he moves on to the missing user ID, so it is not clear whether he endorsed the point.

statement: Student proposal: because a hash cannot be reversed (two different emails can collide), the hash must be stored in the users table.
detail: The teacher did not adopt this reason. He answered that you can instead apply the hash function in the where clause (where hash(email) = the given hash). The hash column was added later for a different reason: so it can be indexed and the lookup avoids a full table scan.
speaker: student (proposal)
verbatim: So we have to have a hash stored because in it, we cannot go in a reverse way from email.

statement: Spotting the problem in a very simple query is hard, like writing a single print statement and asking why your program is not running.
detail: Said after a student could not find what was wrong with the second update of the mark-active transaction (the missing user ID check).
speaker: teacher
verbatim: it's like literally wrote one print tab and you say why my program is not running
flags: check: "one print tab" probably "one print statement"
